Samsung36.gate1_irp_source: IrpTransmogrifier IrpProtocols.xml @c945e76 L2409-L2411 (verbatim; identical in the 1.2.14 release), whose documentation cites elektrolab.wz.cz/katalog/samsung_protocol.pdf. Corroborated by IrpTransmogrifier's own hardware captures of a Samsung Blu-ray remote (see gate 2a) and, for the DB's bit order and E nibble, by the SwiftRemote database itself: its Samsung BD remotes carry UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT/OK/PLAY at exactly the hexcodes those captures' decodes predict
Samsung36.gate2a_structural_vector: bengtmartensson/IrpTransmogrifier @c945e76 src/test/teaserfiles/Samsung36.ict and Samsung36.exp: eight captures of a Samsung Blu-ray remote (Teaser, hifi-remote.com forum), each with the decode IrpTransmogrifier's own test expects. Not vendored (a GPL-3.0 repository, the files used there by permission of the capture's author); tools/misc_capture_audit.py --irpt DIR re-runs the comparison. All 8 keys' bits decode, by a threshold decoder written from the frame layout, to the .exp fields and re-encode to the same bit pattern. A capture carries instrument bias, so this verifies layout, bit order and framing, not absolute durations: capture durations are 0.84-1.00x the encoder's (the unit is nearer 500 us than the IRP's 560) and the frame period is 1.13x (122 ms against ^108m). Independently, crankyoldgit/IRremoteESP8266 @1e2f0f3 src/ir_Samsung.cpp L59-L63 and L175-L190 (sendSamsung36, marked 'Works on real devices') uses a 4515/4438 us header, 512 us bit marks, 490/1468 us spaces, a 512/4438 us divider after 16 bits and MSB-first bits at 38 kHz -- the same frame, with a unit near 500 us, though it calls its own gap 'just a guess'
